skills.name: Timeline Severity/Date Filter Logic
skills.capability: Implements a pure filtering function that narrows an array of incidents by severity level(s) and/or a date range, and wires it into the dashboard's incident-listing API endpoint via query parameters.
skills.prompt_template: You are implementing incident timeline filtering for Pulseboard's internal dashboard API. Write a pure function filterIncidents(incidents, filters) that supports filtering by one or more severity values and/or a startDate/endDate range, and expose it through the existing GET /api/incidents endpoint via severity, startDate, and endDate query parameters. Do not mutate the input array, and treat omitted filters as no-ops so unfiltered requests behave exactly as before.
acceptance_criteria: filterIncidents(incidents, {severity}) returns only incidents whose severity is in the requested set
filterIncidents(incidents, {startDate, endDate}) returns only incidents whose createdAt falls within the inclusive range
GET /api/incidents?severity=SEV1&startDate=...&endDate=... returns 200 with a JSON array containing only matching incidents

skills.name: Dashboard Timeline Filter UI

testcases.name: builds query string from filter state

skills.capability: Renders severity checkboxes/dropdown and a date-range picker on the internal dashboard timeline view, and translates the selected filter state into a query string for the filter API.
skills.prompt_template: You are building the filter controls for Pulseboard's internal dashboard timeline. Add severity multi-select and date-range picker UI above the incident timeline, and implement buildFilterQueryString(filters) that serializes the current filter state into a URL query string consumed by GET /api/incidents. Changing any control should refetch the timeline with the new filters applied, and clearing all filters should restore the unfiltered view.
acceptance_criteria: buildFilterQueryString({severity, startDate, endDate}) returns a query string containing only the provided, non-empty filter values
Selecting a severity or date range re-renders the timeline showing only matching incidents
Clearing all filters restores the full unfiltered incident list

skills.name: Component Category Grouping Model
skills.capability: Extends the component data model/seed data with a category field (e.g. API, Web, Infrastructure) and provides a function to group components by that category.
skills.prompt_template: You are adding categorical grouping support to Pulseboard's component data. Add a category field to the component schema and seed data (values like API, Web, Infrastructure) and implement groupComponentsByCategory(components) which returns an object keyed by category, each holding the array of components in that category, preserving input order within each group.
acceptance_criteria: groupComponentsByCategory(components) returns an object whose keys are the distinct category values present in the input
Each category's array contains exactly the components with that category, in original order
Seeded component data includes a non-empty category value for every component

skills.name: Public Status Page Grouped Tiles UI
skills.capability: Renders public status page component health tiles grouped under category section headings instead of a single flat list.
skills.prompt_template: You are updating the Pulseboard public status page to organize component health tiles by category. Consume the grouped component data (from groupComponentsByCategory) and render each category as a labeled section containing its component tiles, preserving each tile's existing health-status styling. Categories with no components should not render an empty section.
acceptance_criteria: Public status page renders one section heading per distinct component category present in the data
Each component tile appears exactly once, under its correct category section
A category with zero components does not render an empty section on the page

skills.name: Incident History Export Logic & API

testcases.name: serializes incident history to JSON string

skills.capability: Converts an array of incident history records into CSV and JSON text and exposes an export endpoint on the dashboard API that returns a downloadable file in the requested format.
skills.prompt_template: You are implementing incident history export for Pulseboard's internal dashboard. Write toCSV(incidents) and toJSON(incidents) pure functions that serialize resolved incident history records, and add a GET /api/incidents/export?format=csv|json endpoint that streams the result with the appropriate Content-Type and Content-Disposition headers for a file download. Default to JSON when format is omitted or invalid.
acceptance_criteria: toCSV(incidents) returns a header row plus one comma-separated row per incident with matching field order
toJSON(incidents) returns a valid JSON string that parses back into the original array
GET /api/incidents/export?format=csv returns 200 with Content-Type text/csv and a Content-Disposition attachment header

skills.name: Dashboard Export Trigger UI
skills.capability: Adds an export control to the internal dashboard's incident history view that lets the user choose CSV or JSON and downloads the file from the export API.
skills.prompt_template: You are adding an export trigger to Pulseboard's internal dashboard incident history view. Add a control offering CSV and JSON options that, on click, requests GET /api/incidents/export with the chosen format and triggers a browser file download of the response. Respect any currently applied severity/date filters by including them in the export request.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking the CSV export option downloads a file with a .csv extension containing the current history list
Clicking the JSON export option downloads a file with a .json extension containing the current history list
The export request includes any active severity/date-range filters so the downloaded file matches the visible timeline
